description:
Energy can't be created or destroyed. It's one of the most tested rules in physics, and no experiment has ever broken it. Yet the universe is full of energy: stars, galaxies, light, and matter itself. And as space expands, the oldest light in the universe loses energy while dark energy keeps growing. So where did all that energy come from, and does the universe break its own rule? In this physics documentary, we look at what energy really is and follow the discoveries that answer the question. We start with Julius Robert Mayer's observations of sailors' blood and James Joule's experiments, then move to Einstein's E = mc² and Emmy Noether's theorem, which explains why energy is conserved at all. From there, we see how general relativity changes the rule in an expanding universe, why dark energy behaves like a stretched rubber band, and how cosmic inflation may have turned the energy of an early field into the hot Big Bang. We also cover the matter–antimatter puzzle, the zero-energy universe idea, and the open questions cosmology still can't answer.

---

Which idea surprised you the most: that energy conservation comes from the laws of physics not changing over time, that ancient light loses energy without it going anywhere, or that inflation may have created the matter around us from a growing field? And if scientists could solve just one remaining mystery, which would you choose: why matter beat antimatter, or what came before inflation? Share your thoughts in the comments.
